articles.title: Firms told to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law
articles.description: The government argues the change will help jobseekers and could help to prevent pay discrimination.
articles.summary: Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.
key_points: The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible".
It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination.
However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable.

articles.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
articles.description: Investors have reacted to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry.
articles.summary: Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in the US and Asia in a stock market rout after the US midterm elections sparked concerns of a slowdown in artificial intelligence development.
key_points: Shares in firms across the tech and AI sectors plummeted following Democratic wins after election campaigns run on slowing AI.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index closed down by more than 5.5%, losing an estimated $2.5tn (£1.9tn) in market value, according to Dow Jones data, while other key US stock indexes also saw big…
The sell-off comes on top of broader concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off.

articles.title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'
articles.description: Investment has surged into the making of jet turbine blades - an extremely difficult component to make.
articles.summary: Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.
key_points: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.
And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.
During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the…

articles.title: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
articles.description: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.
articles.summary: Interest rates have risen for the first time in more than three years and the Bank of England has signalled a further increase is likely unless the US-Iran war is resolved.
key_points: Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on oil prices.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither…
The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings.

articles.title: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
articles.description: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
articles.summary: People riding drunk or dangerously on e-bikes – and those who jump red lights - could face on-the-spot fines under plans to curb anti-social behaviour.
key_points: Firms which run shared e-bike schemes will also be expected to manage their fleets better and provide designated parking areas to keep pavements safe.
They could also be required to take out insurance so people can claim compensation if they are hit by someone on a shared bike.
It's part of a crackdown on what ministers called the "wild west" of e-biking – with a patchwork of rules across the country often leaving the streets unsafe for pedestrians.

Rate-setters at the Bank make changes to interest rates to fulfil their role of keeping price rises at a steady level.
Higher rates are meant to encourage people to spend less, reducing demand for goods and services and limiting price rises.

articles.title: Welsh aviation firm AerFin bought in £475m deal
articles.description: The company, which was majority owned by a private equity firm, said it was beginning a "new chapter".
articles.summary: A Newport aviation company, that has grown into a global supplier of aircraft engines, parts and maintenance services, has been bought in a deal worth about £475m.
key_points: Japanese firm ORIX Aviation has agreed to acquire AerFin, which employs more than 230 people and operates from sites in the UK and around the world.
Founded by Bob James, AerFin has developed from a south Wales business into a global aviation aftermarket specialist.
Announcing the takeover, AerFin described it as the start of a new chapter for the company.

articles.title: Second buyer makes rescue bid for Poundland as retailer faces collapse
articles.description: A little-known investment group has made a bid to buy the business.
articles.summary: A second buyer has made a rescue bid for Poundland as the discount retailer teeters on the brink of collapse, with thousands of jobs at risk.
key_points: London-based Xyra Group has offered to pay off half of Poundland's outstanding debts - a key sticking point in takeover talks so far - immediately.
With Poundland close to collapse, US-based owners Gordon Brothers have already rejected a rival bid from an Irish property group which would have saved its 12,000 staff.
Gordon Brothers said the business has faced years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable".

articles.title: PepsiCo: Stronger supply chains start on the farm
articles.summary: The multinational food and drink business has long-been investing into programmes designed to improve agricultural capability across its network.
key_points: Among such initiatives is its annual Global Agro University – an event that links its value chain together to share agricultural know-how and experiences.
September’s Hannover-based event focused specifically on potatoes – a key ingredient for PepsiCo’s crisps brands.
Growers, suppliers, agronomists, researchers and industry experts from across 35 countries joined together for classroom learning, technical discussions and practical field demonstrations.

articles.title: Food, fuel and taxes – can the Democrats actually make life cheaper?
articles.description: Their message on cost of living resonated with voters. Now they must show they can deliver.
articles.summary: 'Hopefully things get done': Americans react to historic political shift Two business owners, half a country apart, want the same thing for different reasons.
key_points: In Texas, Kim Hanks, who owns Tillies, a hotel, restaurant and spa business near Austin, says rising grocery and fuel costs are forcing her to raise wages for her 300 staff.
"It's been such a moving target for us on affordability," she told the BBC World Service.
In Indiana, Danny Reynolds, who runs Stephenson's of Elkhart, a clothing and bridalwear store, simply wants Washington to get its act together.

articles.title: Pound rises to its highest level since the Brexit referendum
articles.description: Pound reaches highest level against a basket of currencies since the Brexit referendum a decade ago.
articles.summary: The pound has risen to its highest overall level since the Brexit referendum over a decade ago.
key_points: Sterling has risen notably in recent weeks against the euro and the dollar, ahead of an expected rise in interest rates.

The most-watched measure of the value of the British currency against a basket of 18 of the world's main currencies this week reached its joint highest level since the June 2016 referendum, according…
The value reached 86.4 on an index where 100 equals the value in 2005.

articles.description: The brand's 38 physical stores and online site will continue to operate while receivers review its operations.
articles.summary: Australia's oldest department store, David Jones, has gone into voluntary administration David Jones, Australia's oldest department store chain, has gone into voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk.
key_points: It comes after years of financial struggles for the 188-year-old retailer - known locally as DJs - as customers desert traditional shops for online shopping.
David Jones's physical and online stores will continue to operate while receivers FTI Consulting review the company, said voluntary administrators McGrathNicol.

articles.title: Elon Musk's millions failed to deliver Republican wins in fierce midterms
articles.description: Musk spent nearly $500m in the 2026 US midterm elections, an individual election spending record.
articles.summary: Elon Musk spent almost $450m (£334m) – more than anyone ever has in an election cycle – to back Republican political candidates in the US midterm races.
key_points: It was not enough to keep Democrats from a resounding victory .
Among the most striking wins went to Democrat James Talarico, who beat Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat in Texas.
Musk spent at least $45m in support of Paxton, according to a BBC analysis of campaign finance data .
